req.title: load_logged_in_user populates g.user
req.statement: The system shall populate flask.g.user with the User row for the authenticated session on every request.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that load_logged_in_user must populate g.user with the User row for authenticated sessions on every request. We test: (1) positive - authenticated user has g.user populated with correct user data accessible via a protected endpoint; (2) negative - unauthenticated session has g.user=None causing redirect; (3) boundary/STC - state transition from logged-in to logged-out clears g.user; (4) DT - multiple users each get their own correct g.user row; (5) BVA - session with invalid/nonexistent user_id yields g.user=None. Each test uses exact-value assertions to kill mutations on comparisons, constants, and boolean logic.

tests.name: test_load_logged_in_user_authenticated_populates_g_user
preconditions: User Rahul (id=1, password=stone) exists in DB
actions: Inspect response for 200 and content showing authenticated state
expected: Response body contains username Rahul (proving g.user was populated)
trace: R-FLASKR-029: load_logged_in_user reads session['user_id'] and sets g.user to the DB row
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

# Login as Rahul (id=1)
r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
assert r.status_code == 302
assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'

# GET / triggers load_logged_in_user; if g.user is populated, the page renders 200
r2 = client.get('/')
assert r2.status_code == 200
# The index page shows the logged-in username
assert b'Rahul' in r2.data

def test_load_logged_in_user_authenticated_populates_g_user():

    with app2.app_context():

    c = app2.test_client()

    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'
    r2 = c.get('/')
    assert r2.status_code == 200
    assert b'Rahul' in r2.data

tests.name: test_load_logged_in_user_no_session_g_user_is_none
actions: GET /create without logging in (login_required checks g.user is None)
expected: This proves g.user was None (login_required redirects when g.user is None)
trace: R-FLASKR-029: when session has no user_id, load_logged_in_user sets g.user=None
login_required decorator redirects to auth.login when g.user is None
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_load_logged_in_user_no_session_g_user_is_none():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    # No login: anonymous request to protected endpoint
    r = client.get('/create')
    # login_required redirects to /auth/login when g.user is None
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'
    # Also verify the index page itself returns 200 (not a server error)
    r2 = client.get('/')
    assert r2.status_code == 200
    # Rahul's name must NOT appear (no user logged in)
    assert b'Log Out' not in r2.data

tests.name: test_load_logged_in_user_after_logout_g_user_cleared
preconditions: User Anjali (id=2, password=cloud) exists in DB
actions: GET /create to verify g.user is now None (redirect to login)
expected: Authenticated GET / returns 200 with Anjali in body
trace: R-FLASKR-029: state transition logged-in->logged-out must clear g.user on subsequent requests
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_load_logged_in_user_after_logout_g_user_cleared():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    # Login as Anjali
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Anjali', 'password': 'cloud'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'
    # Authenticated: index shows Anjali
    r2 = client.get('/')
    assert r2.status_code == 200
    assert b'Anjali' in r2.data
    # Logout clears session
    r3 = client.get('/auth/logout')
    assert r3.status_code == 302
    assert r3.headers['Location'] == '/'
    # After logout g.user must be None: /create redirects to login
    r4 = client.get('/create')
    assert r4.status_code == 302
    assert r4.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_load_logged_in_user_correct_user_row_per_session():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    c1 = app.test_client()
    c2 = app.test_client()
    # Login Rahul on client1
    r = c1.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    # Login Anjali on client2
    r2 = c2.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Anjali', 'password': 'cloud'})
    assert r2.status_code == 302
    # client1 sees Rahul
    page1 = c1.get('/')
    assert page1.status_code == 200
    assert b'Rahul' in page1.data
    # client2 sees Anjali
    page2 = c2.get('/')
    assert page2.status_code == 200
    assert b'Anjali' in page2.data
    # Cross-check: Anjali not in client1 page header nav, Rahul not in client2
    # (both usernames may appear in posts, so check Log Out link context)
    assert b'Log Out' in page1.data
    assert b'Log Out' in page2.data

tests.name: test_load_logged_in_user_invalid_session_user_id_yields_none
preconditions: Session is manually set with a user_id that does not exist in DB
actions: GET /create to check if g.user is None (redirect expected)
expected: Proves that when DB lookup returns None, g.user=None and login_required redirects
trace: R-FLASKR-029: if user_id in session has no matching DB row, g.user must be None
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_load_logged_in_user_invalid_session_user_id_yields_none():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    # Inject a session with a nonexistent user_id
    with client.session_transaction() as sess:
        sess['user_id'] = 99999
    # load_logged_in_user will query DB, get None, set g.user = None
    r = client.get('/create')
    # login_required sees g.user is None and redirects
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'
    # Index page should still render 200 (no server error)
    r2 = client.get('/')
    assert r2.status_code == 200

tests.name: test_load_logged_in_user_every_request_repopulates_g_user
actions: Each must return 200 with James visible (g.user repopulated each time)
expected: All three GET / requests return exactly HTTP 200
James appears in all three responses
No request returns 302 or 500 (g.user not lost between requests)
trace: R-FLASKR-029: 'on every request' clause - g.user must be populated for each individual request
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_load_logged_in_user_every_request_repopulates_g_user():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'James', 'password': 'river'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'
    # Three consecutive requests - g.user must be repopulated each time
    for i in range(3):
        resp = client.get('/')
        assert resp.status_code == 200, f'Request {i+1} failed: {resp.status_code}'
        assert b'James' in resp.data, f'James not found in request {i+1}'
    # Verify protected route also works consistently
    r_create = client.get('/create')
    assert r_create.status_code == 200
